edaa62ba169f6744bf5796eea829fe3b17f6b24a.summary: Lets a repo contributor or reviewer agent check a branch diff against main for documentation drift in both directions: which docs a code change should have updated (generated regions, identifier sources, prose pages), and whether changed docs still match source, the canonical-home table in AGENTS.md, the docs/README.md map, and the site audience rule. It names git diff and git grep steps, the make docs-check, make docs-generate, prettier and site build gates, and reports a Blocking/Advisory triage table. It is read-only by design (the report is the deliverable, no silent fixes) and holds no repository facts of its own; it does not cover code defects, which it leaves to review-adversarial.

70a1e916336521886c91307d1435d25dc52df08a.summary: A short checklist for a repo-level security reviewer auditing Kubernetes admission control manifests: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, MutatingWebhookConfiguration, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy. It covers failurePolicy and timeouts, namespaceSelector/objectSelector exemptions, binding scope, CEL failure handling and message leakage, caBundle/HTTPS and NetworkPolicy ingress to the webhook, and mutating risks such as sidecar injection, reinvocationPolicy, CEL side effects and execution order. It is read-only review guidance applicable to any cluster or manifest, part of the review-security-k8s-* family; it does not state exclusions.

1b68dc239230282af96d98dc3efd365e6b2de22a.summary: A repo-level review skill for a contributor or review agent, run as a sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main. It is a read-only checklist applied to manifests and agent configs: one dedicated ServiceAccount per agent, an API audit policy that captures agent requests at Metadata or RequestResponse level, logging to stdout/stderr rather than local disk, no hostPath mounts of /var/log/containers or /var/log/pods, and application-level logging of full prompts, outputs and tool input/output with sensitive data scrubbed first. It does not run any command, targets no specific cluster or fleet, and does not state exclusions.

7d788018b2f1c0766dccaf822865a016a000d671.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading Kubernetes manifests of AI agent workloads. It is a read-only checklist: authenticated outbound calls must go through an injecting credential proxy or sidecar, the main agent container must not receive Secrets via env, envFrom or volume mounts, no plaintext keys in manifests, automountServiceAccountToken false with the token only in the sidecar, a dedicated non-default serviceAccountName, and no wildcard verbs or resources in RBAC. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions.

9759a6166d75c67220e37226c26e9d6bbb484a2b.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading Kubernetes configuration of AI agent workloads. It is a read-only checklist on three fronts: egress NetworkPolicies that must be restrictive with no 0.0.0.0/0 and allowlisted to internal services and the LLM API, outbound routing through an egress gateway or proxy (service mesh, HTTP_PROXY) for inspection and SNI allowlisting, and RBAC or volume mounts that give broad get/list/watch on secrets and configmaps. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions; its egress checks overlap with review-security-k8s-agents-firewall.

f7c35b454b96e422504285594800af48cf3143d8.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading NetworkPolicies and firewall configuration for AI agent control loops and execution sandboxes. Read-only checklist: default-deny egress with a minimal allowlist, blocking agent access to internal cluster APIs and the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254 on its credential ports (TCP 80 pre-NAT, 988 post-NAT) while leaving port 53 open for Cloud DNS for GKE, flagging 0.0.0.0/0 egress, restricting ingress to trusted upstreams, and flagging LoadBalancer or NodePort exposure without ingress NetworkPolicies. It names no commands or cluster scope; the only stated exclusion is that port 53 to the metadata address is not flagged.

6637413a4d35bb967d292206f00ad2f4dbd55097.summary: A repo-level orchestration skill for a contributor or review agent; it is itself a sub-agent of review-security-k8s-main. It takes the project context produced by review-security-k8s-understand, launches six sub-skills in parallel (sandbox, firewall, credentials, prompt-injection, data-exfil, audit-logs), requires each to return a fixed JSON findings shape, triages findings against the context (for example dropping egress-proxy findings for an air-gapped sandbox, or root-in-sandbox findings when a gVisor or Kata RuntimeClass is confirmed) and merges them into one JSON array. It performs no checks of its own, runs no commands, and does not state exclusions.

201fc18e358b726e480e98c3afb95db1fa6ecf4a.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading AI agent deployment configuration. It is read-only and holds only two checks: require an LLM-specific API gateway or WAF sidecar and flag raw agent APIs exposed to untrusted traffic, and ensure system prompts or safety instructions kept in ConfigMaps or environment variables cannot be altered by less privileged workloads. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions; despite the description it has no input-sanitization check.

844e5d24bb3fc74089c5db22460f483543db5572.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, run by a reviewing agent against manifests in a pull request or a cluster, read-only) that audits the execution sandboxes an LLM agent uses to run untrusted code (Python REPLs, bash tools, WASM). It checks three things: a hardened RuntimeClass (gVisor or Kata) instead of a standard pod, separation of the sandbox from the main agent loop plus restrictive seccomp/AppArmor profiles, and ephemeral lifecycles with low CPU, memory and ephemeral-storage limits. It is one of six sub-skills launched by review-security-k8s-agents-main and does not state exclusions.

80472c42ec82b676bade0c5c07ea4a335e3186de.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits Kubernetes Gateway API objects: Gateway, HTTPRoute, TCPRoute, TLSRoute and ReferenceGrant. It flags overlapping hostnames or paths that let one route hijack another, cross-namespace route or secret references without a narrow ReferenceGrant, weak TLS listener settings, missing allowedRoutes namespace restrictions, and wildcard or overly broad hostnames. It is one of ten sub-skills launched by review-security-k8s-main; it covers Gateway API only (classic Ingress is left to review-security-k8s-network) and does not state exclusions.

ab02aaf0895eecad3220be8673a595d4384c9389.summary: A repo-level orchestrator skill (under .agents/skills, read-only) that runs a general Kubernetes security review: it first invokes review-security-k8s-understand for project context, then launches ten sub-skills in parallel (rbac, nodes, network, gateway, namespaces, service-accounts, storage, admission, pod, and agents-main), each told to emit a fixed JSON findings schema with agent, message, file and line. It then triages the raw findings against the context (for example dropping hostPath warnings for CSI daemonsets, or downgrading NetworkPolicy warnings when a strict service mesh exists) and merges them into one JSON array. It performs no checks itself and does not state exclusions.

89c61f081bb00659a031913afe4eecd1bc3e2f95.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits how namespaces are used as isolation boundaries. It flags most workloads piled into one namespace, mixing of trust levels or tenants, custom workloads in default/kube-system/kube-public/kube-node-lease, namespace names that impersonate system components, labels or annotations that bypass policy (OPA exemptions, pod-security enforce=privileged), absurd ResourceQuotas or LimitRanges, suspicious namespace finalizers, cross-namespace references without ReferenceGrant or via ExternalName, and leftover Secrets, ServiceAccounts or RoleBindings in namespaces with no pods. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main and does not state exclusions.

f9732861f5f9b5d9dfc8c6be0eaa8e6693edfee8.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits Kubernetes network isolation and exposure: NetworkPolicies, Services, Ingresses and service mesh policy. It requires default-deny ingress and egress NetworkPolicies per namespace, flags missing egress limits and broad CIDRs or empty selectors, flags public LoadBalancers, NodePort services and exposed admin ports (22, 3389, 2379, 10250), requires TLS and HTTPS redirects on Ingress, flags hand-written Endpoints/EndpointSlices and hostNetwork: true, and for Istio-style meshes requires STRICT PeerAuthentication and default-deny AuthorizationPolicies. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main; Gateway API objects are left to review-security-k8s-gateway, and it does not state exclusions.

4e75a14e2485ef9e69bf96e7ce25ce71981a2ebe.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits ways a compromised pod or node could escalate to cluster-wide control. It flags hostPath mounts of kubelet credentials (/etc/kubernetes, /var/lib/kubelet, kubeconfig) and of container runtime sockets (docker.sock, containerd.sock), extra RBAC bindings for system:nodes or system:node:<name> that bypass NodeRestriction, roles granting impersonate on system:nodes, service-account roles that can create/update/patch/delete nodes or nodes/status, and broad tolerations (operator: Exists with no key) that let untrusted workloads land on control-plane nodes. It recommends ValidatingAdmissionPolicies as the fix for hostPath abuse. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main and does not state exclusions.

6b377b7ab9991eeb230fa5d2f8c62463fa0efd09.summary: Repo-level review skill (run by a contributor or by the review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads Pod specs and their PodSecurityContext/SecurityContext and flags: privileged, host namespaces (hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC/hostUsers), hostPath volumes, allowPrivilegeEscalation, root execution, added capabilities, missing capabilities.drop ALL, missing readOnlyRootFilesystem and seccomp, use of the default ServiceAccount, token automounting, Secret-based SA tokens, and images not pinned by digest. Read-only manifest review, cluster-agnostic, single resource type (Pods and pod templates). Does not state exclusions, though it does not cover RBAC, network, or storage settings beyond hostPath.

e3ddc6a1df2581dbe7b899d0764e3dab85c27398.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding manifests and flags: bindings to system:anonymous/unauthenticated/authenticated/masters and system:serviceaccounts groups, cluster-admin grants, write access to system: bindings, escalation paths (bind/escalate/impersonate, writes to rbac.authorization.k8s.io, CSRs, webhooks, CRDs, tokenreviews, namespaces, networkpolicies), wildcards, deletecollection, over-scoped ClusterRoleBindings, self-modification, and access to secrets, pods/exec, pods/portforward, pods/attach, nodes/proxy, ephemeralcontainers and status subresources. Ships resources/gke-rbac.md, a copy of the GKE RBAC best-practices page with kubectl/jq detection commands and the gcloud --no-enable-insecure-binding-system-* flags. Read-only manifest review, single cluster, GKE-flavoured. Does not state exclusions.

365975fcb74ff19064b839ee7bd799772fdc4289.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads ServiceAccount objects and their bindings and flags: RBAC bound to the default ServiceAccount, one ServiceAccount shared by several apps, automountServiceAccountToken not set to false on the ServiceAccount, several workloads mapped to one GCP identity through the iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account Workload Identity annotation, long-lived kubernetes.io/service-account-token Secrets, imagePullSecrets with broad registry access, and ServiceAccounts with bindings but no workloads. Read-only manifest review, single cluster. Does not state exclusions; RBAC rule content and Pod-level security contexts are covered by sibling skills, not here.

ef19df02a4bd984a40f89a7f0233c038ecc06864.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads StorageClass, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, volume and volumeMount definitions and flags: writable mounts missing readOnly, subPath on user-writable volumes, hostPath use (recommends local PVs), missing fsGroup, ReadWriteMany access mode, StorageClasses without encryption at rest (CMEK or encrypted parameter), Recycle and unmanaged Retain reclaim policies, allowVolumeExpansion without ResourceQuotas, and CSI Secrets Store mounts without strict limits. Read-only manifest review, single cluster, cloud-agnostic. Does not state exclusions.

e8845553d36fbc37a6c14068032c6bb97d7e4e55.summary: Repo-level context-building skill run first by the review-security-k8s-main and review-security-k8s-agents-main orchestrators (and cited in docs/architecture/03-security-model.md). It reads the target project's README, diagrams and architecture docs, names the main components and workloads, labels each workload Infrastructure (CSI drivers, ingress controllers) or Application (APIs, databases), and records global compensating controls such as a service mesh enforcing mTLS or cluster-wide OPA/Gatekeeper policies. Output is a short summary that the orchestrators use to triage sub-reviewer findings. Read-only, no checks of its own; it explicitly leaves specific security reviews to the specialized skills.

463356c7994ddf76da332b2a256598c9e29e1abc.summary: Repo-level skill for a contributor reviewing SKILL.md files in this repository. It checks frontmatter (description opens with the user's action and names its object; YAML-safe values), structure (top-level # Task and # Checks or # Workflow sections, terse headers), prose (no persona setup, no filler, imperative bullets starting with Flag/Require/Ensure) and formatting (single-sentence rules, no loss of checks or domain knowledge when shortening). AGENTS.md and .agents/rules/documentation.md point to it as the style owner for SKILL.md files. Read-only review of skill text; it does not cover placement by persona or whether a skill's checks are correct.

a5d2a04330b74e31be109842c7875c502a3afc57.summary: Platform Agent skill (shipped only on a `next`-mode install with the A2A bus) for the `a2a topics list|read|write` CLI: discover provisioned topics and their class (state vs journal), read standing state such as `upgrade-readiness` while relaying provenance and treating exit 2 as 'empty', write topics the profile owns with `--text`/`--data` and task/context/correlation ids, and append dated findings to the shared `annotations` journal. Read and write, fleet-level shared state. It explicitly excludes task status (stream replay), private memory, scratch notes, topics not in `a2a topics list`, and installs without `NATS_URL` or where the shell sandbox has no `a2a` binary.

c5a9c6ebdc888364b5253d30b13d998b57b4be80.summary: Platform Agent plugin skill (installed into the `platform` profile via the gke-stockout-investigator AgentPlugin) that handles a GKE autoscaler stockout alert from Pub/Sub end to end: send a `send_notification`, check for an open PR on `platform-agent/remediate-stockout-<workload>` with `vcs.py proposal list --source`, confirm the stockout is live via `kubectl get/describe pod`, take a GitOps working copy with `submit_suggestion.py prepare`, run quota/reservation/`kubectl top`/`gcloud beta compute advice capacity[-history]`/`cluster-autoscaler-status` diagnostics, apply eight ComputeClass debugging rules (A-H), edit ComputeClass or workload YAML with remediation comments, commit, and open the PR with `submit_suggestion.py submit --body-file`. Fleet-facing but one alert and one cluster per run; GitOps write, never a live-cluster mutation. It explicitly forbids `execute_code`, forge CLIs, `git add .`, `--body`, and branch-name suffixes.

af7c18b7e669f424dbcade7bb3d4ead3f54c7dac.summary: Cluster Agent, read-only, single cluster and one namespace (or one kind in it). Runs /opt/data/scripts/stall_report.py (agents/platform/scripts/stall_report.py), which applies four heuristics (generation-lag, stale-condition, repeating-warnings, dangling-reference) over kubectl get output for Gateways, HTTPRoutes, Deployments, custom resources and other namespaced kinds, with age thresholds and --kind/--threshold-minutes/--json flags, then records the finding on the kanban card via kanban_complete (including the Session KV controller-stall card format). It explicitly excludes failing-pod and bad-event symptoms (those go to gke-workload-troubleshooting and gke-reliability), never patches, opens PRs or reads Secret contents, and notes that Secret-typed references are unchecked under the default read-only identity.

ea230abd5592e45b3367a8cd235c078df6e24f8d.summary: A short how-to on configuring GKE storage: writing a StorageClass for the Persistent Disk CSI driver, choosing between the PD, Filestore and Cloud Storage FUSE CSI drivers, creating a ReadWriteMany PVC, and expanding a volume by editing the PVC. Every workflow is a create-or-apply write and there are no diagnostic commands, so it reads as configuration guidance rather than single-cluster debugging. Sits under the Cluster Agent; a longer upstream-synced copy with the same name lives under agents/platform/skills. Does not state exclusions.

ddb9a2fcd480a8686e77076696e36ab24531bb02.summary: Cluster Agent, read-only, single workload in one namespace. A five-step SOP: acquire project, cluster, workload and a one-hour time window; read pod and Deployment status and classify Pending, CrashLoopBackOff (exit 137 vs other), ContainerCreating; read namespace events with kubectl get events or gcloud logging read and match FailedScheduling, FailedMount, image-pull failures (with a git log search for the last working tag); read current and previous container logs for OOM, stack traces, egress timeouts and read-only-filesystem errors; check Service endpoints and NetworkPolicies; then record the RCA and a proposed YAML patch on the kanban card with kanban_complete. It explicitly excludes applying patches, opening PRs (submit-suggestion is the Platform Agent's) and passing findings through the chat reply.

8abec4d9d057c6f3a149dd60c80f60e9f94be0b2.summary: Platform Agent, read-only diagnosis and design, project and region scope rather than one cluster. Checks regional quota (gcloud compute regions describe), reservations, live node and pod usage (kubectl top), Spot and Flex-Start obtainability (gcloud beta compute advice capacity, capacity-history) across zones, and future reservation windows for deadline-bound TPU or VM batch jobs (gcloud beta compute advice calendar-mode); records each check with record_evidence (or an Evidence section when the tool is absent), attaches ComputeClass, NAP, ProvisioningRequest and Kueue LocalQueue manifests with attach_artifact, requires a three-path On-Demand/Spot/Flex-Start report, and lists eight ComputeClass resilience rules (fallbacks, large shapes, disk generation mix, On-Demand floor, regional scarcity, quota exceeded, priority starvation, Hyperdisk compatibility). It explicitly excludes creating clusters, applying manifests, opening PRs and handling inbound stockout alerts, which it sends to the gke-stockout-investigator plugin skill.

3d8a18947f466c37c3add5b60ac1c38c93861115.summary: Platform Agent skill that authors Config Connector (KCC) v1beta1 manifests for Google Cloud resource changes and submits them as a pull request through submit-suggestion (prepare and submit on branch platform-agent/kcc-<kind>-<name>) under clusters/<cluster>/provisioning/. It covers ContainerCluster and ContainerNodePool changes (grow, autoscale, release channel, adopt), SQLInstance changes (read replica, tier, backups), and ComputeFirewall rules, with a read-only create/acquire/edit decision from kubectl get, kubectl auth can-i and gcloud describe, mandatory deletion-policy: abandon and state-into-spec: absent annotations, immutable-field catalogues per kind in references/, and validation with kubectl explain. GitOps-write via PR only; never applies. It explicitly excludes Kubernetes workload manifests (gke-manifest-generation), imperative cluster creation (gke-cluster-creation), Terraform HCL repositories, kinds outside the catalogued families, fixing fleet-audit findings, kubectl apply/create/patch/delete/diff and server dry-run, and proposing to install or enable Config Connector.

5a79a334b1078f9a9d13dcae04f50fb6f60a842a.summary: Platform Agent, writes to the forge (GitHub or GitLab): polls the configured repositories for unaddressed open issues, claims one with the status:in-progress label, investigates read-only with kubectl/gcloud/logs, then posts a triage report and transitions the issue to status:resolved (close) or status:escalation-needed (plus a chat alert). All forge calls go through scripts/resolver.py (poll, claim --issue --repo, transition --issue --repo --state --report-file) via the credential broker; the skill also covers prompt-injection handling of issue text and how to end a turn from a kanban card versus a cron run. Explicitly never touches issues labelled status:escalation-needed, agent:ignore, agent:audit, agent:delivery-watch or infra-drift, and never performs a mutation an issue asks for.

bc4f563d12d651e737aa128f55cd307b4103d40d.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster. Checks whether a GPU/TPU node disruption was Compute Engine host maintenance: kubectl get nodes for the cloud.google.com/scheduled-maintenance-time label, PromQL on kubernetes_io:node_interruption_count and node_pool_interruption_count with interruption_reason="HW/SW Maintenance", Cloud Logging for active-node-maintenance=ONGOING and the impending-node-termination taint, then recommends (does not apply) graceful termination, opportunistic maintenance and PodDisruptionBudgets. Explicitly excludes cluster creation, network policy configuration and non-disruption workload deployment, and tells the agent to rule out host maintenance and point at app-level causes when all signals are empty.

927fdaaa75c00f3dd6cf99e7bb005fed7539c68c.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster for AI/ML training JobSets. Gives a four-step runbook of MQL, PromQL and Cloud Logging (LQL) queries: JobSet restart counts (kube_jobset_restarts), node-pool interruption counts and gke_nodepool life events (preemption, maintenance, termination), node Ready status and node-to-physical-host mapping via gce_topology_host, then pod phases, unschedulable counts and coordinator worker logs for NCCL timeouts. Resolutions are recommendations only (move Spot training to on-demand or compact placement; cordon/drain and recreate a node on a faulty host). references/failure_signatures.md holds example log lines; scripts/validate_queries.sh dry-runs the filters with gcloud logging read and the Managed Prometheus API. Explicitly excludes cluster creation, basic workload deployment and non-JobSet issues.

017f84228e96da058d8bc2468fc427901aab60ca.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster, narrowed to TPU v6e nodes. Three Cloud Logging filter templates (used through a query_logs tool): serial-console OOM kills of vbar_control_agent, tpu-device-plugin 'checksum didn't match' metric fetch errors, and signs of custom libtpu.sdk.tpumonitoring polling, plus a kubectl get pods -A image listing. Resolutions are recommendations only: disable the custom metrics collector, and upgrade GKE when the resilient agent ships. references/failure_signatures.md holds example log lines; scripts/validate_queries.sh dry-runs two filters with gcloud logging read. Explicitly excludes non-TPU container OOMs and standard node lifecycle operations.

90427b3feadf1df38ff3db1cf99dca3034c93ae9.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; a write path for one cluster. Covers first-time onboarding of an application to GKE: assess the app, write a Dockerfile (or use Cloud Native Buildpacks), build and push to Artifact Registry (gcloud auth configure-docker, docker build/push, gcloud artifacts docker images describe --show-package-vulnerability), generate a Deployment plus ClusterIP Service manifest with probes and resource limits, then deploy with the GKE MCP tools apply_k8s_manifest / get_k8s_rollout_status / get_k8s_resource or kubectl apply as fallback. assets/ holds a sample Node.js app (Dockerfile, index.js, package.json) and a hardened deployment.yaml that SKILL.md itself does not reference. Explicitly excludes general cluster administration and upgrades, pointing to gke-basics and gke-upgrades, and defers autoscaling, observability, security and reliability to other gke-* skills.

247e90ba74e37349353ea1873962b039fe849373.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; a write path for one cluster. Covers first-time onboarding of an application to GKE: assess the app, write a Dockerfile (or use Cloud Native Buildpacks), build and push to Artifact Registry (gcloud auth configure-docker, docker build/push, gcloud artifacts docker images describe --show-package-vulnerability), generate a Deployment plus ClusterIP Service manifest with probes and resource limits, then deploy with the GKE MCP tools apply_k8s_manifest / get_k8s_rollout_status / get_k8s_resource or kubectl apply as fallback. assets/ holds a sample Node.js app (Dockerfile, index.js, package.json) and a hardened deployment.yaml that SKILL.md itself does not reference. Explicitly excludes general cluster administration and upgrades, pointing to gke-basics and gke-upgrades, and defers autoscaling, observability, security and reliability to other gke-* skills.

64631b4d51059b92cecf1fc390a236964a855f6a.summary: Platform Agent skill for Backup for GKE. It gives the gcloud beta container backup-restore commands to enable the BackupRestore addon, create backup plans (with --include-volume-data, --include-secrets, retention, cron or RPO schedules, CMEK), trigger manual backups, create restore plans and run and verify restores. It is a write skill on one GKE cluster at a time, with restore-safety rules on conflict policies and a rule to confirm before restoring into production. It explicitly does not cover database backups and does not cover the broader Google Cloud Backup and DR service.

4d5fe751c9aabf16be7f2bb4f4ee8318c6846d54.summary: Platform Agent skill for running batch and HPC work on GKE. It gives manifests for Kubernetes Jobs, JobSet, Kueue ClusterQueue and LocalQueue, and Kubeflow MPIJob, the kubectl install lines for Kueue and the MPI Operator, a gcloud node-pools create command for compact placement on Standard clusters, and cost rules (Spot via ComputeClass, scale-to-zero, backoffLimit, checkpointing, maintenance exclusions). It writes workloads into a single cluster. A local footer requires loading capacity-obtainability before scheduling GPU/TPU jobs with a deadline. It explicitly excludes standard web application deployments (gke-app-onboarding) and defers Spot-fallback YAML to gke-compute-classes.

c8a595cffbfc79c91bf3e0e30d3f3e9a5e8bbb17.summary: Platform Agent skill for the GKE Cluster Autoscaler, Node Auto Provisioning and node pool auto-creation. It covers enabling autoscaling (gcloud node-pools and clusters update flags), tuning (autoscaling profiles, location policy, consolidation delay), reading cluster-autoscaler-visibility logs, and diagnosing scale-up failures (stockouts, quota, IP exhaustion, cooldown cascade) and scale-down blockers, with two scripts (log-autoscaler-events.sh tails Cloud Logging; find-scale-down-blockers.sh scans pods, PDBs and nodes with kubectl) and a CapacityBuffer example. It mixes read-only diagnosis with cluster-level write commands on a single cluster. It explicitly defers ComputeClass YAML, schemas and priority configuration to gke-compute-classes.

57c9d2c1f75b42653f6b3a87166e814b9bacbed4.summary: Platform Agent provisioning skill that creates GKE clusters from five templates (golden-path Autopilot, Autopilot dev/test, Standard regional, L4 GPU inference, A3 Hypercompute), each as a gcloud command and a create_cluster MCP payload, with a workflow (discover, gather inputs, choose mode, confirm, create, track with get_operation, verify with get_cluster) and rules to warn about Standard mode, Day-0 choices, cost and quota. Local footers require creating the Cluster Agent profile (python3 /opt/data/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py create) right after creation, deleting it at teardown, and loading capacity-obtainability before recommending GPU/TPU capacity. It is a write skill at project scope. It explicitly excludes application onboarding and deployment configuration (gke-app-onboarding).

20df61b9b68800e88563cad3e724bcd045f70d5a.summary: Platform Agent skill for authoring, tuning and debugging GKE ComputeClass objects: priorities with Spot, reservation, DWS FlexStart and On-Demand fallbacks, GPU and TPU targeting, machine families, location policy, activeMigration and consolidation, the dynamic-rwo StorageClass for stateful PVs, Autopilot mode on Standard clusters, Karpenter migration, and access control via RBAC plus a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. It ships fifteen example YAML assets (labelled EXAMPLE TEMPLATE - DO NOT DEPLOY), ten reference files and a copy of log-autoscaler-events.sh identical to the one in gke-cluster-autoscaler. It writes cluster-scoped CRDs on a single cluster. It explicitly excludes cluster-level Node Auto Provisioning configuration and general cluster creation.

9298ec65c9e48df5e721bcb3866c022cd495737d.summary: Platform Agent skill (agents/platform/skills, upstream google/skills copy) for answering GKE cost questions. It explicitly does not cover live cluster operations, pod troubleshooting (gke-workload-troubleshooting), or cluster provisioning (gke-cluster-creation), and it does not apply manifests to a cluster.

5ffeceb2d6f2ae5dbf8568b50686eb06084581e8.summary: Lets an agent design and configure core GKE cluster networking: it states golden-path values for GKE cluster fields (privateClusterConfig.enablePrivateNodes, masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig, controlPlaneEndpointsConfig.dnsEndpointConfig.allowExternalTraffic, networkConfig.datapathProvider=ADVANCED_DATAPATH, clusterDns=CLOUD_DNS, autoIpamConfig, maxPodsPerNode), shows `gcloud container clusters get-credentials --dns-endpoint|--internal-ip` for private-cluster access, `gcloud container clusters create-auto` with bring-your-own `--network/--subnetwork` and secondary ranges, explains VPC-native (Alias IP) benefits, gives Pod/Service CIDR sizing rules per maxPodsPerNode, and lists Cloud NAT egress options; it names the gke MCP tools get_cluster, update_cluster, apply_k8s_manifest, get_k8s_resource. It explicitly does not cover application ingress, load balancing or Service/Gateway networking (deferred to gke-service-networking), and defers NetworkPolicy manifests to gke-workload-security and gke-multitenancy. It is a reference of settings and single commands, not a troubleshooting procedure, and it contains no Kubernetes manifests.

847870034985ca5547dfed90839b087cca3f4ee6.summary: Lets an agent verify and change platform-level GKE cluster security with gcloud: a golden-path table of cluster fields (workloadIdentityConfig.workloadPool, secretManagerConfig with rotation, rbacBindingConfig.enableInsecureBindingSystem{Authenticated,Unauthenticated}=false, shieldedInstanceConfig secure boot and integrity monitoring, workloadMetadataConfig GKE_METADATA), then `gcloud container clusters describe/update` recipes for --enable-secret-manager with rotation interval, auditing rbacBindingConfig, --binauthz-evaluation-mode=PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE, --enable-shielded-nodes, GKE Sandbox enablement, --database-encryption-key with the Cloud KMS IAM grant to the GKE service agent, and --security-posture / --workload-vulnerability-scanning. It also covers the five predefined roles/container.* IAM roles with when to use each, the GKE service agent and a dedicated minimal node service account (monitoring.metricWriter, logging.logWriter), RBAC best practices audited via check_k8s_auth / get_k8s_resource or kubectl auth can-i, and `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding` patterns giving a GSA storage.objectViewer, cloudsql.client or pubsub.subscriber. It explicitly excludes Workload Identity GSA-to-KSA binding (gke-workload-identity), workload-level controls such as SecretProviderClass, Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy and runtimeClassName gvisor (gke-workload-security), private cluster and Dataplane V2 settings (gke-networking), and enterprise RBAC planning (gke-multitenancy).

b2200519c204a0cd1d79cb22d15527e2aed750ee.summary: Lets an agent verify and change cluster-level GKE security settings with `gcloud container clusters describe/update` and the `gke:get_cluster`, `k8s:check_k8s_auth`, `k8s:get_k8s_resource` MCP tools: a golden-path defaults table (`workloadIdentityConfig`, `secretManagerConfig` with rotation, `rbacBindingConfig.enableInsecureBinding*`, Shielded Node secure boot and integrity monitoring, `GKE_METADATA`), enabling the Secret Manager add-on (`--enable-secret-manager`, `--secret-manager-rotation-interval`), checking insecure `system:authenticated`/`system:unauthenticated` bindings, enabling Binary Authorization (`--binauthz-evaluation-mode`), Shielded Nodes (`--enable-shielded-nodes`) and GKE Sandbox, the five predefined `roles/container.*` IAM roles, the GKE service agent and node service account, and project-level `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding` grants for a GSA (`roles/storage.objectViewer`, `roles/cloudsql.client`, `roles/pubsub.subscriber`); the repo overlay appends `--database-encryption-key` (Cloud KMS secrets encryption) and `--security-posture` / `--workload-vulnerability-scanning`. It explicitly does not cover Workload Identity bindings (gke-workload-identity), workload-level controls such as SecretProviderClass manifests, Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy and `runtimeClassName: gvisor` (gke-workload-security), private cluster and Dataplane V2 networking (gke-networking), or enterprise RBAC planning (gke-multitenancy).

ec1f243ca7f0d9f4ea744e8b7f81f2e1f53a278b.summary: An orchestrator (meta-skill) for productionizing a GKE cluster, one application, or a set of applications. It prescribes a discovery phase (`gcloud container clusters describe` for Autopilot vs Standard and release channel; `kubectl get deployment/namespace/pods/hpa/pdb/networkpolicy` for resource requests and limits, probes, Pod Security Standards labels, dedicated ServiceAccounts), then mandates delegating to `gke-app-onboarding`, `gke-workload-scaling`, `gke-observability`, `gke-reliability`, `gke-workload-identity`, `gke-platform-security`, `gke-workload-security`, `gke-backup-dr`, `gke-service-networking`, and `gke-cost-optimization`, and ends with a RAG status per area plus an overall readiness score, asking the user before any state-changing step. It explicitly does not cover deep single-domain implementation (HPA/VPA tuning, Workload Identity setup, network policy authoring, Backup for GKE configuration, Gateway/Cloud Armor, rightsizing) and holds no domain procedures of its own; it is read-only assessment plus routing.

8da01a8a9123af25edef8a67ad227dca7e8f8ea2.summary: Lets an agent produce environment-specific GKE upgrade artifacts for one cluster at a time: an upgrade plan (sequential control-plane minor path, skip-level node pools, 2-minor skew rule, dev-to-prod progression with Rollout Sequencing), pre/post-upgrade checklists (references/checklists.md), and runbooks built from `gcloud container clusters upgrade --master|--node-pool`, `gcloud container node-pools update --max-surge-upgrade/--max-unavailable-upgrade`, `--enable-blue-green-upgrade` soak tuning, maintenance window and exclusion flags (`--add-maintenance-exclusion-name/-start/-end/-until-end-of-support/-scope`), and PDB backup/relax/restore steps (references/runbook-template.md). It covers release-channel strategy (Rapid/Regular/Stable/Extended, 14/24-month support), exclusion scopes and their 90-day/3-per-cluster/48h-per-92-day limits, mandatory GKE override scenarios, surge vs blue-green vs autoscaled blue-green per workload type (stateless, stateful, GPU/TPU with maxSurge=0 and driver/CUDA coupling), maintenance-window pauses, and a 12-step stuck-upgrade diagnosis (PDB ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS=0, Pending pods, bare pods, admission webhooks, PVC attach, long grace periods, `gcloud container operations list`, ZONE_RESOURCE_POOL_EXHAUSTED/QUOTA_EXCEEDED stockouts with credential rotation and DNS endpoint, GPU driver regressions, `get-upgrade-info` paused reasons, NotReady nodes) in references/troubleshooting.md. It explicitly does not cover cluster creation, application onboarding, networking/routing, or security policy (deferred to gke-basics and other gke-* skills), and in this upstream copy it has no executed fleet-wide version or readiness scan (the shipped copy appends a pointer to fleet-upgrade-verification for that).

4c6e3081c5cc005d06f6a5013708d0c5da47a570.summary: Gives the Platform Agent a seven-step, read-only diagnostic for Workload Identity Federation for GKE: classify the error signature from Pod logs and Cloud Logging (403 iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on the target API, 'could not find default credentials', or calls running as the node default service account); check the cluster workloadPool and node-pool workloadMetadataConfig.mode (GKE_METADATA vs GCE_METADATA) with gcloud container clusters/node-pools describe; verify the KSA-to-identity binding for both direct principal binding (principal://iam.googleapis.com/.../svc.id.goog/subject/ns/.../sa/...) and legacy GSA impersonation (iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account annotation plus roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser); search IAM roles on the target resource with gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies or gcloud projects get-iam-policy; check gke-metadata-server DaemonSet health, its logs, 169.254.169.254 connectivity, DNS, network-policy egress and OOM from >3,000 KSAs; handle the legacy 'Invalid form of account ID' case with the iam.gke.io/return-principal-id-as-email annotation; and escalate when logs are missing or the cause is undetermined. It only proposes gcloud add-iam-policy-binding, node-pools update and kubectl annotate commands for a human, never applies them, and a kube-agents appendix tells the agent that the command gate refuses gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy, gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies and kubectl exec, so those steps are handed to the user. It does not cover in-cluster Kubernetes RBAC errors, general workload crashes (gke-workload-troubleshooting), Pod Security Standards or NetworkPolicies (gke-workload-security), or Workload Identity outside GKE.

75a714914c938a382a641ccfc140e52f0ca977ac.summary: Gives a read-only, seven-step diagnostic for Workload Identity Federation for GKE: classify the error signature from Pod logs, gke-metadata-server logs and Cloud Logging deep links (403 iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on the target API, could not find default credentials, calls running as the node default service account); verify the cluster workloadPool and node-pool workloadMetadataConfig.mode=GKE_METADATA with gcloud container clusters/node-pools describe; verify the KSA-to-identity binding for both direct principal binding (principal://iam.googleapis.com/.../workloadIdentityPools/PROJECT_ID.svc.id.goog/subject/ns/NS/sa/KSA) and legacy GSA impersonation (iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account annotation plus roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on the GSA); verify target-resource IAM with gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies; check gke-metadata-server DaemonSet health, OOM eviction above 3000 service accounts, 169.254.169.254 connectivity, DNS (GCE_METADATA_HOST), NetworkPolicy egress (169.254.169.252:988, sts.googleapis.com:443) and startup races; and handle the legacy 'Invalid form of account ID' case with iam.gke.io/return-principal-id-as-email. It proposes gcloud add-iam-policy-binding, node-pools update --workload-metadata=GKE_METADATA, or kubectl annotate commands for a human and never applies IAM, KSA, node-pool or cluster changes itself, escalating to GKE support when logs are missing or the cause is undetermined. It explicitly does not cover in-cluster Kubernetes RBAC (API-server authorization) errors, general workload crashes (gke-workload-troubleshooting), or Pod Security Standards and NetworkPolicy review (gke-workload-security).

1be8de054a510b32235b18032ebe26841e76fe85.summary: Lets an agent scale a GKE Deployment manually (`kubectl scale deployment --replicas`), configure a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler on CPU, memory, External or Prometheus-backed metrics (`kubectl autoscale` or an `autoscaling/v2` HPA manifest from assets/hpa-example.yaml), and configure a Vertical Pod Autoscaler (`gcloud container clusters update --enable-vertical-pod-autoscaling` on Standard, `autoscaling.k8s.io/v1` manifest from assets/vpa-example.yaml, update modes Off/Initial/Auto/InPlaceOrRecreate). It also gives a VPA-based rightsizing workflow (run in Off mode 24h, read `kubectl describe vpa`, apply target*1.2 with a condition/recommendation/risk table) and best practices on resource requests, HPA/VPA metric conflicts, PDBs and HPA stabilization. It explicitly does not cover cluster-level autoscaling (Cluster Autoscaler), static cluster sizing, or node machine types; it is the upstream google/skills source copy for the generated agents/platform/skills/gke-workload-scaling.

7f9bf0fcf8e3c17cd0a298b188bc864118563d4a.summary: Lets the Platform Agent audit a GKE cluster's security posture with `scripts/audit_cluster.sh <cluster> <region> <project>` (gcloud describe + jq checks for Workload Identity pool, NetworkPolicy/Dataplane V2, Shielded Nodes, Binary Authorization, private nodes), then apply workload-level controls: check `networkConfig.datapathProvider` and enable Calico NetworkPolicy enforcement in two steps on non-DPv2 clusters (`--update-addons=NetworkPolicy=ENABLED`, then `--enable-network-policy`), apply the bundled `assets/default-deny-netpol.yaml` to a namespace, run pods under GKE Sandbox with `runtimeClassName: gvisor`, label namespaces with `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted`, mount Secret Manager secrets through the Secrets Store CSI driver (`SecretProviderClass` with `provider: gcp`), and turn on Dataplane V2 `NetworkLogging` (networking.gke.io/v1alpha1). It also retains a legacy Workload Identity GSA-impersonation walkthrough (`roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` binding, `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account` annotation, `assets/workload-identity-pod.yaml`) but tells the agent to load `gke-workload-identity` first. It explicitly does not cover Workload Identity as the primary path (gke-workload-identity), cluster-wide control-plane security, RBAC hardening, Binary Authorization, Shielded Nodes, or enabling GKE Sandbox/platform add-ons (gke-platform-security), nor container securityContext authoring (gke-manifest-generation).

22c8ccb90ed6890269f1eace40fd7c83aa76fd8f.summary: Lets an agent audit a GKE cluster's posture with `scripts/audit_cluster.sh <cluster> <region> <project>` (gcloud describe + jq: Workload Identity pool, NetworkPolicy/Dataplane V2, Shielded Nodes, Binary Authorization, private nodes), then apply workload-level controls: a default-deny NetworkPolicy asset (`assets/default-deny-netpol.yaml`) per namespace plus `gcloud container clusters update --update-addons=NetworkPolicy=ENABLED` on non-DPv2 clusters, a `NetworkLogging` (networking.gke.io/v1alpha1) manifest for Dataplane V2 allow/deny logging, `runtimeClassName: gvisor` for GKE Sandbox pods, `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted` namespace labels, and a `SecretProviderClass` plus CSI volume for Secret Manager secrets. It also still carries a full Workload Identity KSA-to-GSA impersonation walkthrough (create KSA, `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` binding, `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account` annotation, test pod `assets/workload-identity-pod.yaml`). Its description explicitly excludes Workload Identity (route to gke-workload-identity), control-plane security, RBAC hardening, Binary Authorization, Shielded Nodes, and enabling GKE add-ons (route to gke-platform-security); it does not cover container securityContext authoring, Policy Controller/Gatekeeper beyond a one-line mention, or image signing.

a9edacfc7f0041582ff6a09f51512c490693ebab.summary: Lets an agent work one review round on an open pull request: collect unresolved threads, review-body findings and red checks; cross-check them against the PR's Self-Review; triage each as fix, push-back or defer (to an issue or an expected_fail eval case); bracket fixes with red/green evidence; fix the whole class of a finding; re-review non-trivial fixes with review-preflight; push once with Testing, Live validation and Self-Review updated; reply in every thread with proof; and resolve addressed threads. It encodes the kube-agents-bot budget rules: at most two self-requested /review (or /review fresh for a body-only edit) before green, /request-review at the third reviewed commit, no re-read after a green AI Review check, and decline-by-default for later-round Medium findings unless Kind is behaviour on code the PR added. It does not run the review itself (review-adversarial, review-docs-drift, review-preflight do that), does not cover opening the PR, merging (Tide), the eval loop mechanics, or GitHub command syntax (delegated to docs/pull-request-workflow.md and AGENTS.md).

26f9680d28a6a85662dbab1ef0d33dd575431a43.summary: The skill is the repository's adversarial code-review method for a git diff range (`git diff $BASE...HEAD`): a fresh context that did not write the change derives the change's intent, hunts candidates from ten named angles (A line-by-line scan and error-handler audit, B removed behaviour and weakened CI gates, C cross-file consumers and unverified new references, D IAM/RBAC/NetworkPolicy/credential blast radius and pinned GitHub Actions, E reuse, F simplification, G altitude, H AGENTS.md/.agents/rules violations and prose the diff makes false, I scope, Self-Review/Testing/Bug-Fix claims and red-then-green test coverage, J sibling pull requests via `gh pr list`/`gh pr view`), then re-derives each candidate as CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/REFUTED, writes severity-ordered findings (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) with a Fixed or Deliberately-not-fixed disposition that becomes the PR body's Self-Review section. It is used by authors through `review-preflight`, by reviewers through `.claude/commands/pr-review-batch.md`, and by `kube-agents-bot` as the `playbook:` in `.github/kube-agents-bot.yml`. It explicitly holds no plumbing (no subagent spawning, no GitHub-side posting or thread handling), and leaves the exhaustive documentation-drift check to the companion `review-docs-drift` skill, stopping at rules the diff visibly breaks and prose one hop from a hunk.

414fe00f880129e81dd41c8f7ff46e50eb50e1b0.summary: The skill is orchestration plumbing for the pre-PR self-review: it fixes one three-dot diff range against a freshly fetched gke-labs/kube-agents base (refs/kube-agents-base/<branch>), runs `make docs-check` as a mechanical gate, then fans out `review-adversarial` and `review-docs-drift` as concurrent subagents (or `claude -p` headless sessions) with a handoff that withholds the author's intent, plan, and commit-message bodies and forbids the passes from editing the tree. It covers deduping and merging the two passes' output while keeping each pass's own severity scale (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE vs Blocking/Advisory), assigning a disposition per finding to the bar in `.agents/rules/pre_pr_review.md`, re-running only what a fix invalidated, and formatting the result as the PR's **Self-Review** section (passes run, context type, gaps). It explicitly contains no review method of its own, does not state the review requirement (AGENTS.md 'Pull Request Hygiene' does), does not discharge the other local validation checks (prettier, Docker build, go build), and runs no security or skill-quality review passes.

7938ec43750f8b1886fd3ab0c6f592cb4667624d.summary: The skill gives the agent `scripts/vcs.py`, a forge-neutral CLI whose remote verbs (`capabilities`, `identity`, `clone`, `publish`, `proposal create|list|view|comment|update|close|commits|acknowledge`, `issue create|list|view|comment|update|close`, `label ensure`, `remote-branch view|delete`) go over loopback to a credential broker in another container, while all local work (`git log`, `git show`, `git blame`, `git grep`, `git diff`, `git status`, `git branch`, `git commit`, or the JSON wrappers `log`, `show`, `annotate`, `files`, `grep`, `diff`, `status`, `branch`, `commit`, `discard`) runs a credential-free, transport-less git against a working copy that `clone` unpacks from a bundle and `publish` sends back as a bundle. It covers repository history and file-mode queries, branching and committing on `platform-agent/` branches, opening pull/merge requests and later rounds (`publish --advance`), configured base branches (`baseBranch`, `TARGET_NOT_BASE`), reading issue queues with `--labels`/`--without-labels`/`--query`, pagination (`--page`, `truncated`, `commentsTruncated`), spent-branch cleanup, building file links from `capabilities` `fileUrl`, and the meaning of every `FORGE_*`/`BRANCH_*`/`BASE_*` refusal code; it names GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket as forges the broker may or may not serve. It explicitly does not cover repositories outside the install's managed list or one-off reads of large upstream repositories (that is `inspect-repository`), the GitOps workspaces owned by `fleet-audit` and `submit-suggestion`, and any direct `git push`/`git fetch`/`git clone`/`git remote add` or use of `gh`.

f43dac49e19fdc123fb7d92876e624495d7048a0.summary: Lets an agent drive a fresh kube-agents install onto a GKE cluster through `install.sh` in non-interactive mode: detect the operator's GCP project, region, credentials and existing clusters, interview them for the choices that shape the install (cluster, model provider, chat platform, GitOps forge, permission set), preview with `--dry-run` or `--generate-only`, obtain explicit consent for every change to a pre-existing cluster (Workload Identity, CMEK, node-pool migration, NetworkPolicy, gVisor pool), apply, read the JSON report and hand over the terminal access commands. It also covers the GitHub token-minter paths (PEM import via install.sh or ahead-of-time KMS key), GitLab as the GitOps forge (token file, private CA), and the manual Terraform + Helm route for GitHub Enterprise Server. It does not cover upgrading or uninstalling an existing install (it defers to `upgrade-kube-agents` and `uninstall-kube-agents`), nor the token-minter key procedure or flag default values, which it defers to the site docs, `scripts/installer/README.md` and `install.defaults.env`.

c11416411dff39a00f02ee537ab0a865e6fd22c8.summary: Lets an agent tear down a kube-agents install from a GCP project or GKE cluster by running the release-pinned uninstall.sh non-interactively, which drives lifecycle.sh destroy in terraform/examples/full-install against the install's Terraform state in GCS. It covers choosing the release-pinned script or --source-ref, how install.env is located, the pre-destroy asymmetries the engine handles (KMS forget, PlatformAgent finalizer, helm uninstall on a non-created cluster, backup purge, deletion protection), exit codes 1 and 3, and the GitLab Secrets a teardown leaves on a kept cluster. It does not cover installing or upgrading, installs made outside the Terraform engine except by hand-over to an older release, or removing namespaces, CRDs or volumes left on a kept cluster beyond pointing to the site page.

3d58ebd75e52e353b183487dbb3b83ce37887319.summary: Lets an agent upgrade an existing kube-agents install (Platform Agent, operator, chart and Terraform-rendered settings) on a GKE cluster by driving the repo's upgrade.sh: the release-pinned one-liner, the release bundle's own copy, or a checkout. It covers the three upgrade modes (full, harness, operator), the offline --dry-run and the state-backed --plan previews, the --image-tag/--keep-image-tag/--drop-undeclared-values targeting flags, and the install.env discovery rules. It does not cover a first install, an uninstall, or installs that predate the Terraform + Helm engine (those are sent to install.sh or to the release that installed them).

c10e5736e6f4b0e30f68744fa63fe94de76084bb.summary: Lets the read-only Cluster Agent audit one GKE cluster's observability: it reads loggingConfig/monitoringConfig with gcloud describe, checks gmp-system pods, reads workload logs, and gives example Cloud Logging (LQL) queries. For every gap it reports a proposal rather than a change: Managed Service for Prometheus, control-plane metrics, Dataplane V2 observability, each expressed as a Config Connector ContainerCluster field, plus generic advice on structured logging, dashboards/alerts, OpenTelemetry tracing and Cloud Profiler. It does not run any cluster or GCP mutation, does not open PRs, and does not cover harness/kube-agents self-observability (that is kube-agents-observability) or fleet-wide audits.

c3eec25407d71ad16d7269669b1c8dc1d2b963d6.summary: Lets the Cluster Agent audit one GKE cluster and its workloads for high-availability posture and report proposed fixes: whether the control plane is regional and node pools span zones, whether namespaces carry PodDisruptionBudgets, whether Deployments define readiness/liveness/startup probes, whether terminationGracePeriodSeconds and SIGTERM handling are set, whether topologySpreadConstraints spread pods across zones, and whether a maintenance window exists (proposed as a Config Connector ContainerCluster recurringWindow). It is explicitly read-only: every manifest or setting it shows is a proposal for the report, never an applied change. It does not cover disaster recovery, backups, upgrades, autoscaling, or observability.

2790fecd32fc8493bc90232782408a1d9431c146.summary: Lets the read-only Cluster Agent propose scaling changes for workloads on one GKE cluster: a fixed replica count on a Deployment, an autoscaling/v2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler (CPU, memory, External or Prometheus metrics), an autoscaling.k8s.io/v1 VerticalPodAutoscaler with an update mode and per-container bounds, and, through Config Connector ContainerCluster/ContainerNodePool fields, turning on VPA and node-pool autoscaling. It ships two example manifests (assets/hpa-example.yaml, assets/vpa-example.yaml) and a best-practice list (resource requests, no shared HPA/VPA metric, PDBs, HPA stabilization lag, VPA Auto-mode restarts). It never runs kubectl or gcloud: every change is reported as a proposal, and it does not cover diagnosing why a workload is unhealthy, node-level machine shapes, or fleet-wide rollout of the change.

0729b3a5cce6053b844562b39992822d848df227.summary: Lets the read-only Cluster Agent audit one GKE cluster's security posture (Workload Identity, Network Policy / Dataplane V2, Shielded Nodes, Binary Authorization, private nodes via scripts/audit_cluster.sh and gcloud describe) and report hardening proposals as manifests or Config Connector field changes: Workload Identity KSA/GSA setup, Calico enablement on non-DPv2 clusters as two ordered changes, a default-deny NetworkPolicy per namespace, Shielded Nodes, a gVisor node pool plus runtimeClassName, restricted Pod Security Standards labels, Secret Manager CSI SecretProviderClass mounts, and Dataplane V2 NetworkLogging. It never applies a change; it does not cover RBAC hardening, control-plane security flags, Binary Authorization policy authoring, or Policy Controller constraints beyond a one-line recommendation.

fff90d29c0bd37d4ae4d9d2e9ce511b1ed00678a.summary: Lets the Platform Agent create, delegate to, and delete per-cluster Cluster Agent Hermes profiles: it scaffolds a profile with `cluster_agent_profile.py create` at cluster onboarding, deletes it with `delete` at teardown, resolves the profile name with the `get_cluster_profile_name`/`list_cluster_profiles` tools, dispatches single-cluster runtime diagnostics as kanban cards assigned to that profile (one card per cluster with no `parents` for fan-out, polled with `kanban_show`), reads the RCA from the card's `result`/`metadata`, and opens any resulting PR itself via `submit-suggestion`. It also documents the hourly `cluster_agent_reconcile.py` cron (create for every in-scope cluster, prune on definitive NotFound/exclusion/project-left-scope over two clean runs, `fleet_scope.json`, `--require-create-pass` exit codes 3/4, `--dry-run`). It does not cover cluster provisioning or deletion (`gke-cluster-creation`), scope exclusion mechanics (`manage-cluster`), the Cluster Agent's own debugging procedures, or GitOps PR authoring (`submit-suggestion`).

0b2dc57b9822bc2268b0cc830b5db6a9086c75de.summary: Lets the Platform Agent run one of nine registered fleet-audit streams (security/RBAC compliance, upgrade and patch readiness, workload reliability, fleet waste, consistency drift, AI workload security, stockout prevention, GCP networking fabric, GCE compute) end to end: `audit_report.py start` claims the stream and a per-audit workspace, the agent inspects clusters read-only per the stream's governance SOP (usually by running a bundled deterministic collector: collect.py, fleet_drift.py, patch_readiness.py, fleet_waste.py, fleet_stockout.py), writes a schema-validated findings.json with per-check commands, and `audit_report.py finish` publishes exactly one rewritten ledger issue per stream on the GitOps forge, computes the run-over-run delta, auto-promotes up to five critical manifest fixes into narrow remediation pull requests (merge requests on GitLab), answers `/remediate` comments, and handles declared-intent context repositories, partial coverage, held and clean closes, `silent_ok`, and no-forge installs.
